Subject: Post-demo: SDK install, ephemeral auth, and embeddings pipeline — next steps

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciated the clear breakdown of your clinical search use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

1) Sandbox access + data scope
- Can you share a short-lived sandbox account (API key or service account) we can use for PoC? A read-only dataset with a couple of representative patient records is ideal.

2) SDK and sample code
- We'll send a tiny SDK package for Ruby/Go (install + run). If you prefer Node/Python, flag it.

3) Auth approach recommendation (initial)
- For the PoC: recommend ephemeral JWTs minted by your identity service (rotate every 6 hours) with RBAC to limit inference endpoints and embedding writes. We can also accept short-lived API keys during the initial week for faster validation, then move to JWTs.

4) Routing & embeddings/retention
- We'll demonstrate a simple routing policy that directs sensitive patient queries to private deployment (VPC) and non-sensitive QA queries to hosted API to save cost. For relevance, plan to run embeddings at ingest and use a lightweight reranker during query-time.

5) Technical kickoff and timeline
- Proposed: Tech kickoff w/ engineers next Wed (10/15). Ben will coordinate calendar/time.

Action items for you: share sandbox credentials (or an S3 bucket + service account) and the Veridian compliance questionnaire by EOD Tue so we can prep.

Attached: compliance checklist we referenced in-call.

Thanks — happy to iterate this plan.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK install, ephemeral auth, and embeddings pipeline — next steps

Aisha — thanks, and appreciate the compliance sheet. Quick answers + proposed design doc attached:

1) Token lifetime
- 1-hour expiry tokens are fine for the PoC. Shorter TTLs improve safety but increase rotation calls; 1 hour is a good balance. Our SDK supports automatic refresh using a refresh endpoint or a short-lived service token.

2) Compromise recovery / revocation
- For JWTs: we recommend one of two patterns:
  a) Short-lived signing keys + key rotation: rotate the signing key daily and publish the old keys in a JWKS endpoint for a 24–48 hour overlap window. In a compromise, you immediately revoke the signing key and rotate; Redwood stops accepting tokens signed by revoked keys once the token validation check rejects the kid.
  b) Token introspection: if you need immediate revocation, run a light-weight introspection cache in our gateway. On revocation, the introspection result flips to "invalid" and our edge cache invalidates within seconds (adds network calls but supports immediate revocation).

- For API keys: issue short-lived API keys and maintain a server-side allowlist. If a key is compromised, mark it revoked and our routing layer will deny requests immediately. For long-term, move to service accounts + ephemeral JWTs.

3) SDK bootstrap & sample commands
- We'll provide a tiny SDK tarball and the following quickstart (example in bash):
  export RW_HOST=https://api.redwood.ai
  export RW_AUTH_TYPE=jwt
  export RW_JWT=\"<your-jwt-here>\"
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $RW_JWT\" 
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
    -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-embed-1\",\"input\":\"clinical note\"}' 
    $RW_HOST/v1/embeddings

4) Routing + embeddings flow (PoC)
- Ingest: run embedding pipeline at ingest (batch job) and store vectors in your vector store (we tested with Pinecone/FAISS).
- Query: retrieve top-K with dense search, then call Redwood reranker (small cross-encoder) as a re-ranker before returning results to the UI.
- Policy: tag records with sensitivity level; our routing policy will send "sensitive" queries to your private VPC deployment.

Attached: redwood-ephemeral-svc-account-design.pdf — high level of how a short-lived service account + JWKS flow works. Also linked a draft mutual action plan here: https://doc.redwood.ai/mutual-action-plan/VH-2025-034

Next step: Ben will send a calendar invite for the 10/15 tech kickoff and attach the kickoff agenda. If there are any items in the compliance sheet you want us to pre-fill (evidence we can attach), mark them in column B and we'll prioritize.

— Jonas

Attachment: redwood-ephemeral-svc-account-design.pdf (design stub)
